title: cc-http2-framed-stream-adapter-for-openai-compat
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Implement an HTTP/2-framed streaming adapter that maps Redwood's native streaming protocol to the OpenAI Chat Completions request/response shape. The adapter should allow legacy OpenAI-compatible clients to use Redwood endpoints without changing client-side logic while preserving advanced features: incremental deltas, streaming function_call events, structured outputs, finish_reason semantics, and robust backpressure/retry behavior. This ticket covers the runtime adapter, streaming event schema mapping, protocol negotiation, tests, and a controlled canary rollout.

Goals:
- Translate inbound OpenAI-style Chat Completions requests (messages[], functions[], max_tokens, stop, temperature, stream=true) into Redwood internal request model and routing decisions.
- Emit streaming chunks that match OpenAI deltas: {"id","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created", "model", "choices":[{"delta":{...}, "index":0, "finish_reason": null}]} as a best-effort mapping when clients request legacy shape.
- Support streaming function_call output: stream partial function_call.name and function_call.arguments as multiple delta events, then a final 'finish_reason':'function_call' and a non-streamed consolidated call payload when necessary.
- Preserve role/name metadata and structured output markers so downstream routers/observability can attribute tokens to tools or functions for billing and debugging.
- Provide graceful fallback to non-streaming OpenAI-compatible response on clients that cannot consume framed HTTP/2 pushes (detect via Upgrade headers or Accept types).
- Ensure backpressure: if client stalls, apply configurable buffering window + early fallback to non-streaming aggregate response and emit metric events for operability.

Non-goals:
- Full protocol rewrite for HTTP/1.1 SSE (existing proxy handles SSE separately). This ticket focuses on HTTP/2 framed streaming path and compatibility behavior for OpenAI clients over HTTP/2 and gRPC-web where relevant.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts standard OpenAI chat completion request shape and returns compatible streaming chunks for delta tokens per OpenAI chunk schema.
Function calling: partial function_call streaming works end-to-end; downstream function execution receives final consolidated arguments identical to non-streaming calls.
Behavior under client stall: when client unread window exceeds configured limit, adapter falls back to aggregated response and emits a 'stream.fallback' trace event with reason code.
Compatibility test suite passes: 20 scenarios including multi-turn history, assistant->function->assistant flow, stop-sequence edge cases, and max_tokens enforcement.
Load test: sustained 500 QPS streaming with 128 token average response and p99 end-to-end latency within runtime-1.26 SLO on dedicated canary nodes.
Observability: metrics for bytes_streamed, stream_fallbacks, streamed_function_calls, and per-request token attribution available in Console dashboards.
Security: no change to auth model; adapter respects existing RBAC and audit logging.
comments: 2026-02-21: Initial design review with runtime and SDK teams. Decided to use HTTP/2 DATA frames mapped to OpenAI chunk JSON objects separated by \n delimiters to maximize client compatibility.

2026-02-24: Design note: we must stream function_call arguments as a sequence of delta objects (first delta with 'name', subsequent deltas with 'arguments' fragments). This mirrors OpenAI behavior and avoids breaking tool routers that expect incremental JSON string assembly.

2026-02-28: Engineering spike complete. Implemented prototype that converts internal token stream to OpenAI chunk envelopes. Verified that streaming small UTF-8 multibyte tokens does not split grapheme clusters by buffering token boundaries at the tokenizer layer.

2026-03-03: Feedback from SDK team: Node SDK expects SSE-style \"data: {json}\n\n\" framing. We will support both SSE and HTTP/2 framed JSON objects; protocol negotiation via Accept header (application/json vs text/event-stream).
2026-03-07: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127 (adapter + tests). Requesting review from @mira and @samir for kernel-scheduler implications.
2026-03-09: PM review (Kenji): ensure billing attribution for streamed tokens to the model variant used. Added metric tag 'model_variant' and 'streaming_adapter=true' to consumption events.

2026-03-11: QA report: found edge case where client closes connection mid-function_call and adapter retried the request causing duplicate tool invocations. Added idempotency token propagation and at-most-once enforcement on function invocations in the adapter layer.
2026-03-12: Rolling canary deployment planned for 2026-03-14 to 10% of hosted traffic and selected Dedicated pools. Monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/streams/cc-adapter-canary
